real: The company that invented digital cameras goes bankrupt
source: Kodak — the giant that invented the digital camera in 1975 held its own technology back to protect film sales, and eventually filed for bankruptcy in 2012, becoming a cautionary tale about a company that invented the future and then missed it.
fakes: A photography giant that invented a new technology goes bust
A company invents a product that will later kill its main business
An old industry leader files for bankruptcy after missing a revolution

real: A video-rental empire with 9,000 stores is destroyed by a streaming startup
source: Blockbuster — once the dominant video-rental chain with thousands of stores, it famously turned down a chance to buy a small streaming competitor and later went bankrupt, a byword for a giant that underestimated a newcomer.
fakes: A store-based retail chain is wiped out by an online streaming rival
A company that refused to buy a startup is later destroyed by it
A video-rental giant collapses as its business model becomes obsolete

real: A startup that sold pet supplies online vanishes in the dot-com crash
source: Pets.com — the orange-paw dot-com darling that spent millions on Super Bowl ads to sell pet supplies online became a symbol of the bubble, burning through cash and collapsing in 2000 as the internet gold rush turned to dust.
fakes: A flashy internet startup that sells a niche product disappears in a crash
A company that spends a fortune on a big ad campaign goes under
A dot-com era company becomes a symbol of the bubble bursting

real: A company replaces its famous soda, and millions of Americans riot
source: 1985 — Coca-Cola's 'New Coke' relaunch was met with a flood of angry letters, phone calls, and protests so intense that the company reversed course just 79 days later and brought back the original, one of the most famous marketing blunders (and recoveries) in business history.
fakes: A company reformulates a beloved drink and faces a public backlash
Millions of customers protest the change to a household product
A major brand reverses a controversial decision within months

real: A scheme to pay investors with other investors' money becomes a household word
source: The Ponzi scheme — Charles Ponzi's 1920s investment 'plan' paid early investors using new investors' money, promising impossible returns until it collapsed, and the word 'ponzi scheme' has meant 'get-rich-quick fraud' ever since.
fakes: A fraudster pays early investors with money from new victims
An investment plan promising impossible returns eventually collapses
A con artist's scheme gives a type of fraud its name

real: A 'workplace revolution' worth $47 billion collapses before it can IPO
source: WeWork — the co-working 'revolution' reached a $47 billion valuation before its failed 2019 IPO exposed a company that had been burning cash for years with no clear path to profit, becoming a symbol of overhyped startup culture.
fakes: A company with a billion-dollar valuation fails to go public
A startup built on a trendy business model is exposed for losing money
A 'revolutionary' company collapses right before its IPO

real: A $1.75 billion app to make short videos for phones shuts down in six months
source: Quibi — a streaming service that raised $1.75 billion to make short, 'cinematic' videos for phones closed just six months after launching in 2020, one of the fastest and most expensive failures in tech history.
fakes: A billion-dollar app that launches to hype shuts down within a year
A highly-funded startup folds just months after going live
A new video service burns through its funding and disappears

real: A company promises to revolutionize blood tests — then it's revealed the tests never worked
source: Theranos — the startup that claimed a simple blood drop could run hundreds of tests was exposed in 2015 for not actually being able to do so, leading to a fraud conviction of its founder and the collapse of one of the most hyped companies in Silicon Valley.
fakes: A startup claiming a medical breakthrough is exposed for fraud
A company's core product is revealed to not work as advertised
A high-profile founder is convicted after a tech firm collapses

real: A giant energy company vanishes — its books were fake and its execs are arrested
source: Enron — the once-proud energy and trading giant collapsed in 2001 after years of hidden debt and accounting fraud were exposed, taking thousands of jobs, billions in pensions, and the accounting firm Arthur Andersen down with it.
fakes: A major corporation collapses after years of hidden fraud
A company's accounting is exposed as a massive sham
An energy giant's downfall takes its auditors down with it

real: A single trader's unauthorized bets nearly destroy a 200-year-old bank
source: 1995 — Nick Leeson, a trader at Barings Bank, lost over £1 billion in unauthorized bets in the Asian futures market, bankrupting a British bank that had been trading since 1762 — one of the largest losses by a single trader in history.
fakes: One trader's rogue bets bring down a centuries-old bank
A single employee's unauthorized trading loses more than a billion
A historic bank collapses because of a rogue trader

real: A hedge fund run by Nobel laureates loses billions and needs a rescue
source: Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM) — a hedge fund staffed by Nobel Prize-winning economists nearly collapsed in 1998, and the fear that its failure would crash global markets forced a Fed-arranged rescue by major Wall Street banks.
fakes: A fund run by top academics nearly brings down global markets
A hedge fund's collapse requires a rescue by the largest banks
A group of Nobel laureates' investment firm comes within a hair of failing

real: People trade a single bulb for a house — until the whole thing crashes
source: Tulip mania (1637) — in the Dutch Republic, prices for certain tulip bulbs soared to the value of houses before the market collapsed overnight, becoming the classic example of a financial bubble driven purely by speculation.
fakes: A flower becomes worth more than a house before the market crashes
A speculative bubble in a single product bursts overnight
An entire economy goes wild over one exotic good

real: Thousands of internet companies vanish in a matter of months
source: The dot-com bubble — in the late 1990s, investors poured money into internet companies with no revenue, and when the bubble burst in early 2000, trillions in market value evaporated and thousands of tech firms went under in a matter of months.
fakes: A wave of tech companies with no income vanishes in a crash
Trillions of dollars in market value disappear overnight
An investment frenzy in a new industry ends in a sudden collapse

real: A pocket-sized game console outguns the big players and sells 118 million
source: The Nintendo Game Boy (1989) — a simple, low-powered handheld console that many industry experts dismissed, yet it sold over 118 million units and defined portable gaming for a decade, largely thanks to the bundled hit Tetris.
fakes: A modest handheld console outsells its flashier rivals for a decade
A company's 'underpowered' game system becomes a massive hit
A simple portable device redefines an entire industry

real: A Japanese company's new console starts a war with a rival giant
source: 1994 — Sony's PlayStation launched and, against industry skepticism that Sony could make games consoles, it became a global hit and kicked off a fierce, decade-long console war with Nintendo and Sega that reshaped the industry.
fakes: A TV maker enters the game console market and ignites a rivalry
A company's first gaming device becomes a surprise global hit
A new console starts a long battle between gaming giants
